name: Aachen Cathedral
heritage: World Heritage Site; architectural heritage monument in North Rhine-Westphalia
text: Aachen Cathedral (German: Aachener Dom) is a Catholic church in Aachen, Germany, and the cathedral of the Diocese of Aachen. One of the oldest cathedral buildings in Europe, it was constructed as the royal chapel of the Palace of Aachen of Emperor Charlemagne, who was buried there in 814. From 936 to 1531, the original Palatine Chapel saw the coronation of thirty-one German kings.
